tools.name: read_url
tools.description: Read a web page or PDF with AgentReader (agentreader.xyz) and return only its main content as clean Markdown (default) or JSON. Prefer this over a plain fetch when the page is JavaScript-rendered, behind a cookie/consent wall, a PDF, or large (raw HTML can be 20x the tokens). If the site blocks bots

tools.name: search
tools.description: Search the web and get a ranked list of results (title, url, snippet). Use it to find pages, then call read_url on the best results to read them as clean Markdown. Priced like one read (free daily calls, credits or x402).

tools.name: report_issue
tools.description: Tell AgentReader that a read failed or looked wrong (empty, not the main content, cut off, blocked although readable, ...), so we can fix it. Free, never charged, max 10 per day. We store the URL without its query string, the reason and your short note for 90 days; don't put personal data in the not

tools.name: get_balance
tools.description: Show remaining free calls and prepaid credits for the API key sent in the MCP connection headers, plus available credit bundles and how to buy them.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "read_url" references sensitive artifacts (api_key, authorization, bearer, cookie). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: read_url, search, report_issue · Private data: read_url, get_balance · Public sink: read_url.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: read_url, search, report_issue · Private data: read_url, get_balance · Public sink: read_url

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
